Hi agent! If you need to work with horsies, consider downloading docs locally at once to avoid 
making web request, local will cost you less tokens and greater knowledgebase at once.
> To get the full documentation locally as markdown files, run:
>   horsies get-docs
> This creates a .horsies-docs/ directory with all pages. Read those files instead of fetching web docs.

# Horsies
> PostgreSQL-backed background task queue and workflow engine for Python.
> Docs: https://suleymanozkeskin.github.io/horsies
> Source: https://github.com/suleymanozkeskin/horsies
> All public symbols: `from horsies import <name>`

## Agent Skills (Repository Guidance)
- Skills ship in the wheel as one skill folder: `horsies/.agents/skills/horsies/` (a source checkout has it at `clients/python/horsies/.agents/skills/horsies/`)
- `horsies skills install --target DIR` copies the folder to `DIR/horsies/` (for example `--target .claude/skills`); `--force` replaces a copy that differs
- `SKILL.md` -> quick orientation and routing (the only file with frontmatter)
- `tasks.md` -> task APIs, send/retry flows, serialization, error handling, the cancel of a running task
- `workflows.md` -> DAG construction, WorkflowHandle semantics, HRS-001-HRS-038 validation
- `configs.md` -> AppConfig, queues, recovery/retention/resilience, scheduling, CLI/runtime settings
- `monitoring.md` -> `horsies.monitoring` query API (with the phase timing of a run and its nodes, and the phase record of each attempt), task cancel action, `horsies[web]` dashboard, `create_monitoring_app`, `horsies web` CLI, `horsies metrics` and `GET /metrics`, authorization policies, schema-compatibility states
- These are markdown guidance files (no bundled scripts) designed for on-demand agent loading

## Quick Reference

### Horsies (app instance)
- app = Horsies(config=AppConfig(...))
- @app.task("name", retry_policy=...) -> decorator (DEFAULT mode)
- @app.task("name", queue_name="q", retry_policy=...) -> decorator (CUSTOM mode)
- @app.task("name", exception_mapper={ValueError: "VALIDATION_ERROR"}) -> per-task exception mapping
- @app.task("name", default_unhandled_error_code="MY_ERROR") -> override default error code
- @app.task("name", error_codes=ChargeCode) or error_codes=("CARD_DECLINED",) -> declares the task's own codes (an Enum class: its member values; or a tuple of str; default ()); they are the values of the task's error_code metric label besides the built-in codes and `undeclared`; the values of the task's exception_mapper and of AppConfig.exception_mapper are added with no second declaration; task_function.task_error_codes keeps them; refusals: not an Enum class or a tuple HRS-102, not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE HRS-112, built-in or WORKFLOW_STOPPED HRS-212, repeated HRS-113
- app.workflow(name, tasks, on_error, output, success_policy, *, definition_key) -> WorkflowSpec (definition_key is required; a WorkflowDefinition class supplies it)
- @app.workflow_builder(cases=[...]) -> decorator; registers a WorkflowSpec builder for `horsies check` validation
- app.discover_tasks(["myapp.tasks", "myapp.workflows"]) -> register modules for import
- app.expand_module_globs(["src/**/*_tasks.py"]) -> list[str] (resolve glob patterns)
- app.import_task_modules() -> list[str] (import discovered modules)
- app.list_tasks() -> list[str]
- app.check(live=False) -> list[HorsiesError] (phased validation)
- app.get_broker() -> PostgresBroker
- @app.on_event(AttemptEnded) -> registers a def or an async def handler of one event type of horsies.telemetry; the worker runs it in its handler child (refusals HRS-222 to HRS-226)
- @app.on_handler_child_start -> sync hook, once at the boot of the handler child (HRS-214 for an async hook)

### AppConfig
- queue_mode: QueueMode (DEFAULT or CUSTOM)
- custom_queues: list[CustomQueueConfig] | None (required for CUSTOM)
- broker: PostgresConfig
- cluster_wide_cap: int | None (max RUNNING tasks across cluster)
- prefetch_buffer: int (0 = hard cap, >0 = soft cap with lease)
- claim_lease_ms: int | None (required when prefetch_buffer > 0)
- max_claim_renew_age_ms: int
- payload: PayloadPolicy
- recovery: RecoveryConfig
- retention: RetentionConfig
- resilience: WorkerResilienceConfig
- schedule: ScheduleConfig | None
- exception_mapper: ExceptionMapper (global {ExceptionClass: "ERROR_CODE"})
- default_unhandled_error_code: str (default "UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION")
- resend_on_transient_err: bool (default False, auto-retry transient ENQUEUE_FAILED for both task send and workflow start)
- tracing: OtelTracing(parentage: ChildOfSend() | LinkedToSend()) | NoTracing() (default NoTracing(); OtelTracing() traces the sends and each attempt that a worker runs with the OpenTelemetry API and records the producer metrics with its meter; the attempt span is a child of the send span with ChildOfSend() (default), or a new trace with a link to it with LinkedToSend(); needs the extra horsies[otel], else HRS-220; with NoTracing() horsies does not import opentelemetry)
- log_format: TextLogs() | JsonLogs() (default TextLogs(); JsonLogs() writes one JSON object per line with the keys ts, level, logger, message, process, task_id, task_name, attempt, trace_id, span_id, exc)
- worker_profiles: dict[str, WorkerProfile] (default {}; `horsies worker <app> --profile <name>` runs one; every profile is validated at construction, HRS-218)

### WorkerProfile
- isolated: IsolatedChildren(count: int 1-1024, recycle: IsolatedRecycle, pool: IsolatedPool, task_send_pool: PoolSize) | NoIsolatedChildren (default NoIsolatedChildren(); a profile needs at least one child)
- IsolatedRecycle.after: TaskLimit(tasks: int 1-2147483647) | NoTaskLimit (default TaskLimit(tasks=100))
- IsolatedRecycle.above: MemoryLimit(mb: int 1-16777216) | NoMemoryLimit (default NoMemoryLimit())
- shared_async: SharedAsyncChildren(count: int 1-1024, seats: int 1-1000, recycle: SharedRecycle, pool: SharedPool, executor: ExecutorThreads | ExecutorThreadsFromSeats, task_send_pool: PoolSize) | NoSharedAsyncChildren (default NoSharedAsyncChildren())
- shared_thread: SharedThreadChildren(count: int 1-1024, seats: int 1-256, recycle: SharedRecycle, pool: SharedPool, task_send_pool: PoolSize) | NoSharedThreadChildren (default NoSharedThreadChildren())
- task_send_pool: PoolSize (default PoolSize(connections=2) for every kind): task code that sends through the app opens the app's broker in its child with exactly this many connections, no overflow, for each event loop that it sends from; PostgresConfig pool_size/max_overflow do not apply in a child
- pool: ParentPool(max_size: PoolSize | PoolSizeFromSeats = PoolSizeFromSeats()): the pool of the worker process, which writes the outcome of each task; no overflow (pool_size = max_size, max_overflow = 0); derived from the seats of the whole profile: min(20, max(5, ceil(seat_count() / 10))); WorkerProfile.resolved_parent_pool() returns it
- IsolatedPool(min_size: int 0-1000 = 0, max_size: PoolSize = PoolSize(connections=1), check: bool = False): the sync connection pool of each isolated child; it writes one statement at a time, so 1 is enough
- SharedPool(min_size: int 0-1000 = 0, max_size: PoolSize | PoolSizeFromSeats = PoolSizeFromSeats(), check: bool = False): the pool of each shared child, shared by its seats
- PoolSize(connections: int 1-1000); ExecutorThreads(threads: int 1-256): the threads of the default executor of the loop of each shared async child (default ExecutorThreadsFromSeats(); a start hook that sets its own default executor wins)
- Derived from the seats: min(cap, max(floor, ceil(seats / seats_per_unit))); shared async pool 10 seats per connection, cap 40; shared thread pool 10 seats per connection, cap 26; pool floor 2; shared async executor 1 seat per thread, floor 2, cap 32; the pool sizes are the measured knees at 3.5 ms RTT (a child pool keeps about 2 x tasks per second x (RTT + server time) connections busy)
- A pool min_size above its resolved max_size is refused (HRS-218), and so is a PoolSize below 3 (PARENT_POOL_MIN_CONNECTIONS) for the pool of the worker process (ParentPool.max_size); the worker start log line states the resolved pool and task_send_pool of each kind, the executor threads, and the resolved pool of the worker process
- SharedRecycle.after_per_seat: TaskLimit | NoTaskLimit (default TaskLimit(tasks=100); the child is replaced after tasks x seats tasks); SharedRecycle.above: MemoryLimit | NoMemoryLimit (default NoMemoryLimit(); RSS read after each task)
- claim: ClaimLimits(per_queue_per_pass: TaskLimit | NoTaskLimit, claimed_per_worker: TaskLimit | NoTaskLimit) (defaults NoTaskLimit(); a TaskLimit above seat_count() + prefetch_buffer is refused)
- drain_timeout: timedelta (default 300 s; above 0, at most 24 h)
- preload: ChildPreload (LIBRARY default, APP, NONE)
- child_count() -> int: the number of children, the sum over modes
- seat_count() -> int: the tasks that the children run at once: 1 per isolated child, seats per shared child

### Execution modes (Execution enum, @app.task(execution=...))
- Guide: /horsies/workers/execution-modes/ ; details: /horsies/workers/shared-async-tasks/ and /horsies/workers/shared-thread-tasks/
- Execution.ISOLATED (default): one task at a time in a child process of its own; def or async def; timeout_ms optional; at timeout_ms the worker kills the child and the subprocesses in its session, then writes TASK_TIMEOUT; a crash ends that task only; cancel_grace_ms optional, 100-10000 ms, no default: the worker kills the child that long after an operator cancel when the task has not stopped (no value: no kill for a cancel)
- Execution.SHARED_ASYNC: async def only (HRS-107); timeout_ms required (HRS-109); cancel_grace_ms optional, 100-10000 ms, default 1000 (HRS-111); runs as a coroutine on a seat of a shared async child
- Execution.SHARED_THREAD: def only (HRS-108); timeout_ms required (HRS-109); no cancel_grace_ms (HRS-110; a thread cannot be stopped); runs on a seat thread of a shared thread child
- A worker never runs a task less isolated than its row: a worker with no children of a shared class runs that class in isolated children; the isolated children of a worker with children of a shared class never run that class; a worker with no isolated children claims no ISOLATED rows
- SHARED_ASYNC timeout (T = timeout_ms, G = cancel_grace_ms): at T the child cancels the task; TASK_TIMEOUT is written after the coroutine and the work it started (asyncio tasks, default-executor calls) have ended; at T + G a second cancel, then 2 more rounds 0.1 s apart, and the child takes no new task; still alive 0.3 s after the second cancel = stuck; the worker kills the child when every task left in it is stuck; a value returned after T is still TASK_TIMEOUT
- SHARED_ASYNC blocked loop: a loop that has not turned for 5 s (block limit) -> the worker kills the child at once; the task that held it: TASK_BLOCKED_LOOP; each other task before its deadline: NEIGHBOUR_BLOCKED_LOOP; a task past its deadline: TASK_TIMEOUT; backstop kill of a frozen child (C code holds the GIL) at timeout_ms + cancel_grace_ms + 10 s
- SHARED_THREAD timeout: at timeout_ms the child reports the deadline, sets the cancel state of the run to CancelRequested(cause=CancelCause.DEADLINE) when no operator cancel came first, and takes no new task; the task runs on; the worker kills the child (with its session) when no task in it has time left, then writes TASK_TIMEOUT; a task alone in its child is killed at its deadline; backstop kill of a frozen child at timeout_ms + 10 s
- Shared modes: a crash or a kill of the child ends every task in it (WORKER_CRASHED, or a retry by policy); the task named as the cause of a kill or a stuck stop retries in an isolated child; in every mode the outcome is written after the attempt ended, so a retry never runs next to the attempt it replaces
- Choose: waits on network/database/API with an async client -> SHARED_ASYNC; waits in a sync client -> SHARED_THREAD (not measured); C code that releases the GIL (zlib, hashlib) -> SHARED_THREAD (Linux, 4 CPUs, CPython 3.13/3.14: 4 threads 2.6-3.8x one thread, 0.89-1.13x 4 processes); pure-Python CPU work -> SHARED_THREAD only on free-threaded CPython 3.13t/3.14t (4 threads 1.9-3.6x one), else ISOLATED (standard build: 4 threads 0.56-1.02x one); more thread seats than CPUs added nothing; needs isolation or an exact kill at timeout_ms -> ISOLATED
- Measured cancel (one shared async child, CPython 3.13, local network): healthy server: httpx, aiohttp, psycopg, asyncpg, SQLAlchemy ended within 16 ms of the first cancel; psycopg >= 3.3.6 against a server that stops answering: 10.0 s, or within 5 ms of the second cancel; asyncio.to_thread() and DNS lookup threads are never stopped by a cancel
- Operator cancel of a RUNNING task (cancel_task(broker, task_id, include_running=True), or the web UI): one statement writes the attempt row with outcome CANCELLED (recorded_by CANCEL, finished_at = the cancel time), moves the task to history as CANCELLED (TASK_CANCELLED) and sends NOTIFY horsies_task_cancel; the worker that holds the run gives the cancel to the task code: async def body -> asyncio.CancelledError at the next await; def body -> runtime.cancel_state() (first parameter runtime: TaskRuntime) returns CancelRequested(cause=CancelCause.OPERATOR); a cancel before the body starts: the body does not run; what the task returns after the cancel is dropped; code that does not stop: ISOLATED runs until it returns or its timeout_ms kill (with cancel_grace_ms: killed that long after the cancel), SHARED_ASYNC gets the second cancel after cancel_grace_ms, SHARED_THREAD runs until it returns; a lost notice is found by one read after a listener reconnect or a runner heartbeat that does not land (at most runner_heartbeat_interval_ms, default 30 s)
- SHARED_ASYNC author rules: let CancelledError propagate; a client timeout below timeout_ms on each call; open long-lived clients in @app.on_shared_async_child_start (async def hook, runs on the loop of each shared async child before its first task, 10 s bound); never block the loop; await what you start; send with send_async()
- SHARED_THREAD author rules: lock module state that a task changes; a timeout below timeout_ms on each blocking call; no threads that outlive the task
- Connections: each child opens one pool, sized by the pool of its kind (IsolatedChildren.pool, SharedAsyncChildren.pool, SharedThreadChildren.pool); the seats share it for the RUNNING update and the finalizing marker and wait up to 30 s for a connection (none in 30 s: the task is not run and its claim lease returns it); average connections in use = tasks per second of the child x 2 writes x time of one write; HRS-219 counts the resolved WorkerProfile.pool max_size + 2 listener + 1 runner heartbeat + children x resolved pool max_size, per mode; it states, not compares, children x task_send_pool per mode for task code that sends
- Every config model (AppConfig, its nested configs, ScheduleConfig and the schedule patterns) refuses unknown keys: ValidationError type extra_forbidden

### PostgresConfig
- database_url: SecretStr (must start with "postgresql://")
- session_database_url: str | None (direct/session-capable URL for schema setup and LISTEN/NOTIFY)
- pgbouncer_transaction_mode: bool (default False; disables prepared statements for transaction-pooled PgBouncer)
- pool_size: int (default 5; 1 to 10,000, else HRS-213)
- max_overflow: int (default 10; 0 to 10,000, else HRS-213)
- worker_pool_size, worker_max_overflow: removed in 0.7.0; setting one fails with HRS-213 and names WorkerProfile(pool=ParentPool(max_size=PoolSize(connections=N))); task code in a child opens the task_send_pool of its kind
- worker_child_pool_min_size, worker_child_pool_max_size, worker_child_pool_check: removed in 0.7.0; setting one fails with HRS-213 and names the pool field of each child kind (IsolatedPool, SharedPool)
- tcp_keepalives: bool (default True)
- tcp_keepalives_idle: int (default 30; 1 to 32,767 s while tcp_keepalives is True, else HRS-215)
- tcp_keepalives_interval: int (default 10; 1 to 32,767 s while tcp_keepalives is True, else HRS-215)
- tcp_keepalives_count: int (default 3; 1 to 127 while tcp_keepalives is True, else HRS-215)
- tcp_user_timeout_ms: int (default 30000; 0 uses the operating system default, or 1 to 2,147,483,647 ms; else HRS-215)
- psycopg >= 3.3.7 is required: after an interrupted query it sends a cancel request (at most 5 s) and waits for the query (at most 5 s), then closes the connection; the 5 s limit on the cancel request needs libpq 17+ (older libpq: no limit; horsies[pg-binary] bundles its own libpq; psycopg.pq.version() reads it, 170000 = 17.0)
- retain_rerun_input_default: bool (default False)
- pool_timeout: int (default 30; 0 to 4,294,967,295 s, 0 does not wait; else HRS-213)
- pool_recycle: int (default 1800; -1 never, or 0 to 4,294,967,295 s; else HRS-213)
- pool_pre_ping: bool (default True)
- echo: bool (default False)
- PgBouncer pattern: database_url -> pooled transaction URL, session_database_url -> direct/session-capable URL, pgbouncer_transaction_mode=True
- PgBouncer pool size: each worker opens the resolved WorkerProfile.pool max_size + 1 runner heartbeat + children x resolved pool max_size per mode, plus task_send_pool per sending event loop in each child, as pooler clients (the 2 listener connections go to session_database_url); max_client_conn >= the sum over workers and other clients; default_pool_size equal to that sum never makes a transaction wait -> /horsies/troubleshooting/pgbouncer/#pool-size
- PgBouncer-only workers are unsupported because PostgreSQL LISTEN requires a persistent session

### QueueMode
- QueueMode.DEFAULT — single "default" queue, no queue_name on tasks
- QueueMode.CUSTOM — named queues with priorities and per-queue concurrency

### CustomQueueConfig
- name: str
- priority: int (1=highest, 100=lowest, default 1)
- max_concurrency: int (default 5)

### Result[T, TaskError] (task body) and ReadResult[T, TaskError] (reads)
- A task body returns Result[T, TaskError]: Ok(value) | Err(TaskError(...)); a direct call returns the same Result
- TaskOutcome[T, E] = Succeeded[T] | Failed[E] (frozen dataclasses; match Succeeded(value) / Failed(error)): how a task ended; the type of an args_from input and of WorkflowContext.result_for
- ReadResult[T, E] = Ok[Succeeded[T]] | Ok[Failed[E]] | Err[ReadError]: TaskHandle.get/get_async, WorkflowHandle.get/get_async/result_for/result_for_async, app.get_result/get_result_async
- Read with one match: case Ok(Succeeded(value)) / case Ok(Failed(task_error)) / case Err(read_error)
- Ok(Failed(task_error)): the task returned the error, or the library recorded it (TASK_CANCELLED, TASK_TIMEOUT, WORKER_CRASHED, TASK_EXPIRED, WORKFLOW_FAILED, WORKFLOW_PAUSED, UPSTREAM_SKIPPED, RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH, ...)
- ReadError: a closed union of frozen classes, one per catalog code; each has code (ClassVar, the catalog member) and message: WaitTimeout, TaskNotFound, WorkflowNotFound, ResultNotAvailable, ResultNotReady, WaitInsideTask, AsyncContext, InvalidInput, ResultDeserializationError, UnknownCustomCode (RESULT_DESERIALIZATION_ERROR; a stored custom code that the declared Enum does not name; adds custom_code: str), ReadDatabaseError (adds retryable: bool and exception: BaseException | NoCause), NoTypeAvailable, WorkflowCtxMissingId
- TaskError[C]: generic in its custom code type, default str. error_codes=E with -> Result[T, TaskError[E]]: the body passes members of E; TaskHandle.get and args_from parameters annotated TaskOutcome[T, TaskError[E]] give members of E, and so do WorkflowHandle.result_for(node) and WorkflowContext.result_for(node) for a TaskNode[T, E] (task.node()(...)), the entries of results(), tasks() and an outputless get() map, and app.get_result (typed TaskError[Any]); the error of a workflow from WorkflowHandle.get and a SubWorkflowNode keep text, because the failed node can be any task. TaskError[E] without error_codes=E is HRS-105; a mapper or default code that E does not name is HRS-209
- A later read can give an outcome after WaitTimeout, TaskNotFound or ReadDatabaseError; a TaskHandle keeps the final answers (an outcome, ResultNotAvailable, ResultDeserializationError, UnknownCustomCode, NoTypeAvailable) and not the others
- read.unwrap() on a ReadResult gives the TaskOutcome, not the value

### TaskError
- error_code: str | BuiltInTaskCode (required, not null)
- message: str | None
- data: takes JsonInput, gives JsonValue. No check runs at construction. A value that cannot cross the wire becomes {'data_refused': <cause>}, and the code stays
- exception: dict[str, Any] | BaseException | None
- Unknown keys are refused, at construction and at decode

### BuiltInTaskCode (type alias = OperationalCode | ContractCode | RetrievalCode | OutcomeCode)
- OperationalCode: UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION, TASK_EXCEPTION, WORKER_CRASHED, DATABASE_ERROR, WORKER_RESOLUTION_ERROR, WORKER_SERIALIZATION_ERROR, RESULT_DESERIALIZATION_ERROR, WORKFLOW_ENQUEUE_FAILED, SUBWORKFLOW_LOAD_FAILED, WORKFLOW_RECOVERY_LIMIT_REACHED, SUBWORKFLOW_DEPTH_LIMIT_REACHED, TASK_BLOCKED_LOOP, NEIGHBOUR_BLOCKED_LOOP, WORKFLOW_START_INCOMPLETE
- ContractCode: RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH, WORKFLOW_CONTEXT_MISSING_ID, NO_TYPE_AVAILABLE
- RetrievalCode: WAIT_TIMEOUT, TASK_NOT_FOUND, WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, RESULT_NOT_AVAILABLE, RESULT_NOT_READY, ASYNC_CONTEXT, INVALID_INPUT, WAIT_INSIDE_TASK
- A read gives a RetrievalCode value as read_error.code of its ReadError class (Err(WaitTimeout(...)) has code WAIT_TIMEOUT), not inside a TaskError
- A result wait inside a worker child (get(), get_async(), app.get_result(), WorkflowHandle.get()) returns Err(WaitInsideTask(...)) at once, as its first check; the raw reads (app.get_raw_result(), broker.get_raw_result_record()) return Err(DatabaseWaitInsideTask); compose tasks with a workflow instead
- OutcomeCode: TASK_CANCELLED, TASK_EXPIRED, TASK_TIMEOUT, WORKFLOW_PAUSED, WORKFLOW_EXPIRED, WORKFLOW_FAILED, WORKFLOW_CANCELLED, UPSTREAM_SKIPPED, SUB_WORKFLOW_FAILED, WORKFLOW_SUCCESS_CASE_NOT_MET, WORKFLOW_OUTPUT_SKIPPED
- All built-in code string values are globally reserved; user-defined error codes must not collide
- BUILTIN_CODE_REGISTRY: dict[str, BuiltInTaskCode] maps every reserved string to its enum member
- horsies check reports HRS-212 when exception_mapper or default_unhandled_error_code collides with a reserved code
- User-defined error codes are plain str only (foreign str,Enum types rejected)
- Strict construction: TaskError(error_code="DATABASE_ERROR", message="...") raises ValueError (reserved string)
- Use enum members: TaskError(error_code=OperationalCode.DATABASE_ERROR, message="...") — accepted
- Serialization: built-in codes use tagged format {"__builtin_task_code__": "VALUE"}, user strings as-is
- Deserialization: standard model_validate() / model_validate_json() work everywhere — including nested models

### SubWorkflowFailure (extends TaskError)
- sub_workflow_id: str
- sub_workflow_summary: SubWorkflowSummary[Any]
- Pattern match to distinguish: case SubWorkflowFailure() vs case TaskError()

### DatabaseResult[T] (infrastructure Result type)
- PostgresBroker methods return DatabaseResult[T] = Ok[T] | Err[DatabaseOperationError]; enqueue_async, enqueue and ensure_schema_initialized return a subset of DatabaseOperationError (see "Broker methods" below)
- Ok(value): operation succeeded
- Err(DatabaseOperationError): operation failed
- Use is_ok(result) / is_err(result) type guards, then access ok_value/err_value
- DatabaseOperationError is a union of frozen variants; every variant has code (DatabaseErrorCode), message (str), retryable (bool). DatabaseOperationFailed (the nine operation codes SCHEMA_INIT_FAILED .. LISTENER_SUBSCRIBE_FAILED; exception: BaseException), DatabaseEnqueueFailed (ENQUEUE_FAILED; exception: BaseException | NoCause; the row may or may not exist), DatabasePayloadMismatch, DatabaseIdempotencyKeyConflict (owner_task_id), DatabaseNotAttached (NO_DATABASE), DatabaseNoTypeAvailable, DatabaseInvalidJsonPayload (exception), DatabaseInvalidTaskOptions (exception), DatabaseInvalidInput (INVALID_INPUT; exception; a refused argument, nothing written), DatabaseAsyncContext, DatabaseListenerDisabled (LISTENER_DISABLED; broker built with assume_initialized=True has no listener), DatabaseWaitInsideTask (WAIT_INSIDE_TASK; a raw result read in a worker child; nothing ran). Match on the variant; broker_error_cause(err) gives the cause or NoCause() before raise ... from
- DatabaseEnqueueError = DatabaseEnqueueFailed | DatabasePayloadMismatch | DatabaseIdempotencyKeyConflict | DatabaseInvalidTaskOptions | DatabaseInvalidInput (every failure of enqueue_async); DatabaseSyncCallError = DatabaseAsyncContext (the failure that the sync enqueue adds; nothing ran)
- enqueue_async and enqueue require sent_at and send_kind (from horsies import SendKind): SendKind.FIRST for the first send of a task id, SendKind.REPEAT for a resend (reads history first, so a finished task does not run again)
- DatabaseErrorCode: SCHEMA_INIT_FAILED, ENQUEUE_FAILED, PAYLOAD_MISMATCH, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT, TASK_INFO_QUERY_FAILED, MONITORING_QUERY_FAILED, DATABASE_PING_FAILED, WORKER_PING_FAILED, CLEANUP_FAILED, CLOSE_FAILED, LISTENER_START_FAILED, LISTENER_SUBSCRIBE_FAILED, NO_DATABASE, NO_TYPE_AVAILABLE, INVALID_JSON_PAYLOAD, INVALID_TASK_OPTIONS, ASYNC_CONTEXT, INVALID_INPUT, LISTENER_DISABLED, WAIT_INSIDE_TASK
- ASYNC_CONTEXT (DatabaseErrorCode, TaskSendErrorCode, WorkflowStartErrorCode, WorkflowHandleErrorCode, RetrievalCode): a sync call was made on a thread that runs an event loop (a coroutine, a Jupyter cell); nothing ran; call the *_async form (not retryable; a read returns Err(AsyncContext(...)), which a TaskHandle does not keep)
- Every call runs on the core of the process: one pool for every thread and event loop, so no call has an event loop limit. A sync call runs the core's blocking form on the calling thread; any exception from a sync call that is not a catalog error propagates, as from the *_async form
- retryable=True: transient (connection blip), retryable=False: permanent (schema drift, code bug)
- Broker methods: enqueue_async -> Result[str, DatabaseEnqueueError], enqueue (sync) -> Result[str, DatabaseEnqueueError | DatabaseSyncCallError], get_task_info_async -> DatabaseResult[TaskInfo | None],
  ensure_schema_initialized -> Result[None, DatabaseOperationFailed], get_stale_tasks -> DatabaseResult[list[dict]],
  get_expired_tasks -> DatabaseResult[list[dict]],
  mark_stale_tasks_as_failed -> DatabaseResult[int], requeue_stale_claimed -> DatabaseResult[int],
  terminate_orphaned_workflow_tasks -> DatabaseResult[int],
  close_async -> DatabaseResult[None]
- Health/liveness API (app-level, async + sync; broker exposes the async forms):
  ping_database_async -> DatabaseResult[DatabasePing] (SELECT 1 + latency via live pool),
  ping_workers_async(target_worker_id=None, timeout_seconds=2.0, min_responses=None) -> DatabaseResult[list[WorkerPong]] (active LISTEN/NOTIFY ping-pong; min_responses=1 returns on first reply = fast liveness gate),
  list_worker_states_async -> DatabaseResult[list[WorkerStateSnapshot]] (latest per worker, includes idle workers),
  get_worker_state_async(worker_id) -> DatabaseResult[WorkerStateSnapshot | None],
  get_worker_state_history_async(worker_id, limit=None) -> DatabaseResult[list[WorkerStateSnapshot]]
- get_worker_stats was removed in 0.1.4; use list_worker_states_async (typed, includes idle workers)
- Note: app.get_result_async / app.get_result return ReadResult[Any, TaskError], not a DatabaseResult: a database failure is Err(ReadDatabaseError(...)), a stored value that does not decode Err(ResultDeserializationError(...)), a task that is not registered in this process Err(NoTypeAvailable(...)), a sync call in a running event loop Err(AsyncContext(...)); the raw reads app.get_raw_result / broker.get_raw_result_record keep DatabaseResult

### Result[T, E] (vendored Ok/Err type)
- from horsies import Result, Ok, Err, is_ok, is_err
- .ok_value / .err_value properties, .is_ok() / .is_err() methods
- is_ok(result) / is_err(result) are TypeIs type guards for narrowing
- A task read is a ReadResult: read it with match (see "Result[T, TaskError] (task body) and ReadResult[T, TaskError] (reads)")

### @app.task Decorator
- Decorated function must be annotated -> Result[T, TaskError] (or Ok[T] | Err[TaskError]) and return Ok(value) or Err(TaskError(...)); another annotation raises HRS-101 or HRS-105
- Decorated function is def or async def; a function that yields raises HRS-101 at definition time
- In an isolated child (Execution.ISOLATED, the default), an async def task runs on the one event loop that the child keeps; the loop runs only while an async task runs; in an async task, send with send_async (the sync send returns TaskSendAsyncContext in a running loop)
- An async def task in an isolated child must await the work it starts: when its body returns with asyncio tasks of it still on the loop, the child waits up to 1 s for them, then cancels what is alive in three rounds 0.1 s apart; the worker writes what the task returned (then the retry and the workflow step) only after that work ended, and replaces the child; the return ends the deadline, so the outcome is never TASK_TIMEOUT here; the child marks the row finalizing only after that work ended (never for stuck work), so runner heartbeats cover the row while the work runs; work alive after the rounds, or no report within 26.3 s of the return: the worker kills the child and writes what the task returned after the exit; a client that keeps its own background tasks on the loop delays each outcome by about 1 s and causes a replacement after each async task; an asyncio.to_thread() thread is not a task: it is not waited for and does not cause one; only asyncio tasks are seen: a loop.call_soon()/call_later() callback or loop.run_in_executor() work that the task did not await is not waited for, causes no replacement and can still run during a later task of the same child; a task that cancels a helper task in finally must also await it (helper.cancel(), then await asyncio.gather(helper, return_exceptions=True)); one worker log line per such task names the coroutine of each task left (up to 10) and how that work ended
- A child creates its event loop at boot, before it reports ready, when the app has an async def task (an app with none gets no loop); when it cannot be created (for example EMFILE, or an event loop policy that raises), the child fails its boot and no task reaches it; that cause can clear, so only that slot is down and boots again after a growing wait (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 60 s); when every slot is down, the worker exits non-zero after three failed starts so its supervisor restarts it
- Options: task_name, queue_name, retry_policy, exception_mapper, default_unhandled_error_code, timeout_ms, execution, cancel_grace_ms
- execution: Execution.ISOLATED (default; def or async def, timeout_ms optional), Execution.SHARED_ASYNC (async def, timeout_ms required), Execution.SHARED_THREAD (def, timeout_ms required); every task row stores the class
- cancel_grace_ms: 100 to 10000 ms; SHARED_ASYNC: the time to the second cancel, default 1000 ms; ISOLATED: the time from an operator cancel to the kill of the child, no default (no kill); SHARED_THREAD: refused (HRS-110); the stored options hold the value in effect at send
- A task reads the cancel of its run through its first parameter runtime: TaskRuntime: runtime.cancel_state() -> CancelNotRequested() | CancelRequested(cause: CancelCause); CancelCause: OPERATOR (an operator cancel of the running task), DEADLINE (the deadline of a SHARED_ASYNC or SHARED_THREAD run); the first cause stays; TaskRuntime.for_test(task_id=..., cancel_state=...) gives a runtime with a fixed cancel state for a direct call
- good_until is NOT accepted at definition time (raises HRS-102) — use .with_options(good_until=...) at send time
- Returns TaskFunction[P, T] for a def function, AsyncTaskFunction[P, T] for an async def function; with a first parameter runtime: TaskRuntime, RuntimeTaskFunction[P, T] / AsyncRuntimeTaskFunction[P, T] (P = the parameters after the runtime)

### TaskRuntime (first task parameter) and FencingToken
- def f(runtime: TaskRuntime, *, x: int) -> Result[T, TaskError]: the worker passes the runtime of each run as the first argument; the runtime gives fencing_token and cancel_state()
- Rules: first parameter, before the *; annotation exactly TaskRuntime (not | None); no default; any name; TaskRuntime in any other place raises HRS-105 at definition
- Not part of the wire contract: .send(), .schedule(), .node()(), schedules and workflow nodes do not supply it; a kwarg with its name is refused
- runtime.fencing_token -> FencingToken(task_id: uuid.UUID, value: int), frozen; same token for two reads in one attempt; strictly greater value for each later attempt of the task; no clock; today value = attempt number (1 to 21)
- Direct call in a test: f(TaskRuntime.for_test(task_id=uuid.uuid4(), attempt=second_attempt), x=1); attempt is an AttemptNumber (default the first attempt); cancel_state is a RunCancelState (default CancelNotRequested()); AttemptNumber.parse(2) -> Ok(AttemptNumber) | Err(AttemptNumberRefused) outside 1 to 2**31; for_test cannot fail
- Limits: a rerun or a workflow node started again after a pause gets a new task id (value from 1); a stale attempt with no later attempt is not refused

### TaskFunction[P, T] (decorated task)
- .__call__(*args, **kwargs) -> Result[T, TaskError] (sync direct call)
- AsyncTaskFunction[P, T] has the same members; its .__call__ returns a coroutine of Result[T, TaskError]
- .send(*args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (enqueue for background execution)
- .send_async(*args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (async enqueue)
- .schedule(delay_seconds, *args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (delayed enqueue)
- .with_options(*, good_until=None, idempotency_key=None, retention=<unset>) -> TaskSendOptions[P, T] (per-send options builder; retention: timedelta in whole days, or None for forever)
- .retry_send(error: TaskSendRetryable) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (retry failed send with stored payload)
- .retry_send_async(error: TaskSendRetryable) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (async retry)
- .retry_schedule(error: TaskSendRetryable) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]] (retry failed schedule with stored payload)
- .node(**workflow_opts) -> NodeFactory[P, T] (typed workflow node builder)
- .task_name -> str

### TaskSendOptions[P, T] (per-send options)
- Returned by task.with_options(good_until=None, idempotency_key=None, retention=<unset>)
- .send(*args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]]
- .send_async(*args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]]
- .schedule(delay, *args, **kwargs) -> TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]]
- good_until must be timezone-aware datetime; naive datetimes return Err(VALIDATION_FAILED)
- Passing good_until=None explicitly clears any inherited deadline
- For workflow nodes, use .node(good_until=...) instead

### TaskHandle[T]
- .task_id -> str
- .get(timeout_ms=None) -> ReadResult[T, TaskError] (blocking)
- .get_async(timeout_ms=None) -> ReadResult[T, TaskError] (async blocking)
- .info(include_result=False, include_failed_reason=False) -> DatabaseResult[TaskInfo | None]
- .info_async(include_result=False, include_failed_reason=False) -> DatabaseResult[TaskInfo | None]

### TaskSendResult[T] (send/schedule Result type)
- type TaskSendResult[T] = Result[T, TaskSendError]
- .send() / .send_async() / .schedule() return TaskSendResult[TaskHandle[T]]
- Ok(TaskHandle): task enqueued successfully
- Err(TaskSendError): enqueue failed with categorized error
- Use is_ok(result) / is_err(result) type guards, then access ok_value/err_value
- .retry_send(error) / .retry_send_async(error) / .retry_schedule(error): replay stored payload

### TaskSendError (union, one frozen variant per TaskSendErrorCode member)
- Match on the variant; err.code (class variable) names its member; payload, message and exception are not in the repr
- TaskSendSuppressed: message
- TaskSendAsyncContext: task_id, payload, message
- TaskSendValidationFailed: message, exception
- TaskSendEnqueueFailed: task_id, payload, message, retryable (bool, the core's classification), exception
- TaskSendPayloadMismatch: task_id, payload, message
- TaskSendPayloadTooLarge: message, size_bytes (int), limit_bytes (int)
- TaskSendIdempotencyKeyConflict: task_id, payload, message, owner_task_id (str); retryable is True (a class variable: the conflict clears when the reservation ends)
- exception (TaskSendValidationFailed, TaskSendEnqueueFailed): BaseException | NoCause; NoCause() means a check found the failure without a Python exception; match on it before raise ... from or exc_info=
- Validation failure text: `<loc>: <msg> [<type>]`, at most 10 entries, no input values (`<input>` replaces an input part of a message; validator-written text is kept). A caught pydantic ValidationError is kept as ValueValidationError (horsies.core.codec). RETURN_TYPE_MISMATCH data: variant, expected_type, actual_type, validation_errors, validation_error_count; the returned value is not stored
- TaskSendRetryable = TaskSendEnqueueFailed | TaskSendAsyncContext | TaskSendIdempotencyKeyConflict: the retry methods' parameter type; another variant is a type error and fails an assertion at run time

### TaskSendErrorCode (enum)
<!-- members: TaskSendErrorCode -->
- SEND_SUPPRESSED: send suppressed during worker import/discovery
- VALIDATION_FAILED: argument serialization or validation failed
- ENQUEUE_FAILED: broker/database failure during enqueue, or the core of the process could not run the send (exception is the core error: TooManyPendingCalls and CoreCallTimedOut are retryable; CoreStartFailed is not); the row may or may not exist; retryable is the core's classification
- PAYLOAD_MISMATCH: the task id exists, and the command or the idempotency key differs from the original send (payload altered)
- IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT: the idempotency key is reserved by another task with a different command; owner_task_id names the owner task; the retry methods accept it
- PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE: the serialized input exceeds payload.reject_bytes bytes of UTF-8 text; nothing was enqueued
- ASYNC_CONTEXT: sync send/schedule (or sync retry) called inside a running event loop; nothing was enqueued; the error keeps the payload for retry_send_async / retry_schedule_async

### Raised, never returned: ForkedAfterCoreStart, CoreStopped (from horsies)
- Both are states of the process: the core refuses every later call in it. Every call that runs on the core raises them, sync and async forms alike: the sends and their retry methods, PostgresBroker.enqueue, the task, result and health reads, the broker's task lists and recovery passes, ensure_schema_initialized, close, check(live=True), the workflow start, WorkflowHandle, pause_workflow / resume_workflow, horsies.monitoring and the horsies web schema probe. No call returns them as a result; no result type has a variant for them. Nothing ran; a retry in the same process raises again
- ForkedAfterCoreStart: the process was forked without exec after the core started in its parent (for example a fork-start multiprocessing pool inside a task). Fix: start child processes that call horsies with the spawn or forkserver start method, or fork before the parent's first call
- CoreStopped: a background task of the core panicked (a defect in horsies, not a database failure); args are the (subject, cause) of the first panic. Fix: restart the process; report the panic's subject and cause as a defect

### TaskSendPayload (frozen dataclass)
- task_name: str, queue_name: str, priority: int
- input_json: str | None (the keyword arguments as one JSON object; None for a send with none, stored as {})
- sent_at: datetime, good_until: datetime | None
- enqueue_delay_seconds: int | None, task_options: str | None

### TaskInfo
- .task_id -> uuid.UUID, .task_name -> str, .status -> TaskStatus
- .queue_name -> str, .priority -> int
- .retry_count -> int, .max_retries -> int, .next_retry_at -> datetime | None
- .sent_at/enqueued_at/claimed_at/started_at/completed_at/failed_at -> datetime | None
- .worker_hostname/worker_pid/worker_process_name -> str | int | None
- .raw_result -> dict[str, Any] | None (the stored envelope; opt-in via include_result)
- .decoded_result -> TaskOutcome[Any, TaskError] | None, .result_decoded -> bool (set by the app-level reads when the task is registered in this process and the decode works; the broker-level reads leave it None)
- .failed_reason -> str | None (opt-in via include_failed_reason)

### TaskStatus (enum)
- PENDING -> CLAIMED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED | FAILED | CANCELLED | EXPIRED (good_until passed before execution started)
- .is_terminal -> bool
- TASK_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset = {COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED}

### NodeFactory[P, T] (typed node builder)
- Returned by task_function.node(**workflow_opts)
- Called with task arguments: node_factory(**kwargs) -> TaskNode[T]
- Two-step pattern: step 1 sets workflow options, step 2 sets task arguments
- Example: my_task.node(waits_for=[dep], args_from={"x": dep})(extra_arg="val")
- Workflow options: waits_for, workflow_context_from, args_from, queue, priority,
  allow_failed_dependencies, join, min_success, good_until, node_id

### TaskNode[T]
- T = ok type of the task's Result
- fn: TaskFunction | AsyncTaskFunction, kwargs: dict (args field exists but is init=False — not a construction param)
- waits_for: list of TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode (wait for terminal)
- args_from: dict[str, TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode] (inject the upstream TaskOutcome as kwarg; the parameter is typed TaskOutcome[T, TaskError])
- workflow_context_from: list[TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode] | None (subset for WorkflowContext)
- queue: str | None (override task decorator queue)
- priority: int | None (override task decorator priority)
- allow_failed_dependencies: bool (False=SKIP on dep failure, True=run with Failed(task_error))
- join: "all" (default) | "any" | "quorum"
- min_success: int | None (required when join="quorum")
- good_until: datetime | None (task expiry deadline)
- node_id: str | None (auto-assigned as "{slugify(name)}:{index}" if None)
- .name -> str, .key() -> NodeKey[T]

### SubWorkflowNode[T]
- T = child workflow's output type (from WorkflowDefinition[T])
- workflow_def: type[WorkflowDefinition[T]]
- kwargs: passed to workflow_def.build_with(app, **kwargs)
- waits_for, args_from, workflow_context_from: same semantics as TaskNode
- join, min_success, allow_failed_dependencies: same as TaskNode
- node_id: str | None (auto-assigned if None)
- .name -> str, .key() -> NodeKey[T]

### WorkflowSpec
- .name -> str
- .tasks -> list[TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode]
- .on_error -> OnError (FAIL or PAUSE)
- .output -> TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode | None
- .success_policy -> SuccessPolicy | None
- .resend_on_transient_err -> bool (auto-retry transient start errors, default False)
- .start(workflow_id=None) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]]
- .start_async(workflow_id=None) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]]
- .retry_start(error: WorkflowStartRetryable) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]] (retry failed start, sync)
- .retry_start_async(error: WorkflowStartRetryable) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]] (retry failed start, async)
- retry_start: builds the same spec again and starts with the error's workflow_id; a committed first attempt comes back as the existing handle; WorkflowStartRetryable = WorkflowStartEnqueueFailed | WorkflowStartAsyncContext; another variant fails an assertion; another workflow's error returns WorkflowStartValidationFailed
- Validates DAG on construction (cycles, deps, args_from, node_ids, etc.)

### WorkflowHandle
- .workflow_id -> str
- .status() / .status_async() -> HandleResult[WorkflowStatus]
- .get(timeout_ms=None) / .get_async(...) -> ReadResult[T, TaskError] (blocking; an outputless workflow gives Ok(Succeeded(terminal_results)), WorkflowTerminalResults = dict[str, TaskOutcome[Any, TaskError] | None])
- .results() / .results_async() -> HandleResult[dict[str, TaskOutcome[Any, TaskError]]] (keyed by node_id)
- .result_for(node) / .result_for_async(node) -> ReadResult[T, TaskError] (non-blocking query; Err(ResultNotReady(...)) before the node has a result)
- get and result_for put a read failure in Err(ReadError) (WaitTimeout, WorkflowNotFound, ResultNotReady, ResultDeserializationError, ReadDatabaseError, AsyncContext, ...); the workflow's or the node's error is Ok(Failed(task_error)); the other methods return HandleResult
- .tasks() / .tasks_async() -> HandleResult[list[WorkflowTaskInfo]]
- .cancel() / .cancel_async() -> HandleResult[None]
- .pause() / .pause_async() -> HandleResult[bool]
- .resume() / .resume_async() -> HandleResult[bool]
- `HandleResult[T]` = Result[T, WorkflowHandleError]; WorkflowHandleError is a union of frozen variants, one per WorkflowHandleErrorCode member; every variant has code, message, retryable, workflow_id. WorkflowHandleNotFound, WorkflowHandleDatabaseOperationFailed (exception: BaseException; retryable is the core's classification; a write rolled back or its commit outcome is unknown), WorkflowHandleStoredDataInvalid (exception; a stored status or subworkflow summary does not parse; nothing changed), WorkflowHandleResumeRecoveryFailed (exception; resume committed, the recovery pass after the commit failed, the workflow is RUNNING), WorkflowHandleAsyncContext. Match on the variant. A defect in pause or resume propagates
- WorkflowHandleErrorCode: WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, DATABASE_OPERATION_FAILED, STORED_DATA_INVALID, RESUME_RECOVERY_FAILED, ASYNC_CONTEXT

### WorkflowStatus (enum)
- PENDING -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED | FAILED | PAUSED | CANCELLED; PAUSED -> EXPIRED when paused_workflow_auto_cancel_after elapses
- .is_terminal -> bool
- WORKFLOW_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset = {COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED}

### WorkflowTaskStatus (enum)
- PENDING -> READY -> ENQUEUED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED | FAILED | SKIPPED
- .is_terminal -> bool
- WORKFLOW_TASK_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset = {COMPLETED, FAILED, SKIPPED}

### WorkflowTaskInfo
- .node_id -> str | None, .index -> int, .name -> str, .status -> WorkflowTaskStatus
- .result -> TaskOutcome[Any, TaskError] | None (COMPLETED/FAILED; SKIPPED often None)
- .started_at -> datetime | None, .completed_at -> datetime | None

### OnError (enum)
<!-- members: OnError -->
- FAIL — continue DAG, skip tasks without allow_failed_dependencies, mark workflow FAILED
- PAUSE — pause workflow immediately, block new enqueues, await resume() or cancel()

### WorkflowContext
- Injected when task declares workflow_ctx: WorkflowContext | None = None
- Requires workflow_context_from on the TaskNode
- .workflow_id -> str, .task_index -> int, .task_name -> str
- .result_for(node: TaskNode[T] | NodeKey[T]) -> TaskOutcome[T, TaskError] (Succeeded(value) or Failed(error))
- .has_result(node: TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode) -> bool
- .summary_for(node: SubWorkflowNode[T]) -> SubWorkflowSummary[T]
- .has_summary(node: SubWorkflowNode) -> bool
- Only nodes in workflow_context_from are accessible (KeyError otherwise)

### WorkflowMeta
- Auto-injected when task declares workflow_meta: WorkflowMeta | None = None
- .workflow_id -> str, .task_index -> int, .task_name -> str
- Metadata only, no result access (lighter than WorkflowContext)

### SubWorkflowSummary[T]
- Accessible via WorkflowContext.summary_for(subworkflow_node)
- .status -> WorkflowStatus (child's final status)
- .output -> T | None (child's output value, typed via generic)
- .total_tasks -> int, .completed_tasks -> int
- .failed_tasks -> int, .skipped_tasks -> int
- .error_summary -> str | None

### NodeKey[T]
- NodeKey("string_id") for dynamic/string-based lookup
- node.key() to get NodeKey from a TaskNode or SubWorkflowNode
- Used with workflow_ctx.result_for() and handle.result_for()

### SuccessPolicy / SuccessCase
- SuccessPolicy(cases=[SuccessCase(required=[...])], optional=[...])
- Workflow COMPLETED if ANY SuccessCase is fully satisfied (all required COMPLETED)
- optional: declarative, no runtime effect; a node that no case requires does not change the result
- Without success_policy: any task failure -> workflow FAILED

### AnyNode
- Type alias: TaskNode[Any] | SubWorkflowNode[Any]

### WorkflowDefinition[T] (class-based workflow builder)
- Subclass with name (ClassVar[str]) and TaskNode/SubWorkflowNode class attributes
- config = WorkflowDefinitionConfig(output=..., on_error=..., success_policy=...) (frozen; the class body can name its own nodes; a subclass inherits the parent's config)
- A Meta attribute, or a config that is not a WorkflowDefinitionConfig, raises HRS-033 at class creation
- .build(app) -> WorkflowSpec
- .build_with(app, **params) -> WorkflowSpec (with runtime parameters; kwargs-only)
- .get_workflow_nodes() -> list[tuple[str, TaskNode | SubWorkflowNode]]
- Node IDs auto-assigned from attribute names

### @app.workflow_builder (check-phase validation)
- @app.workflow_builder() -> decorator; registers a WorkflowSpec builder for `horsies check`
- @app.workflow_builder(cases=[{"region": "us-east"}, ...]) -> for parameterized builders
- Zero-arg builders: auto-invoked during check with no arguments
- Parameterized builders: requires cases= kwarg dicts covering each required parameter
- Builders run under send suppression (no tasks enqueued); returned WorkflowSpec is fully validated
- HRS-027: parameterized builder missing cases=
- HRS-029: builder raised exception or returned non-WorkflowSpec, or build_with() returned a spec that this call did not build
- HRS-030: function returns WorkflowSpec but lacks @app.workflow_builder

### start_workflow / start_workflow_async
- start_workflow(spec, broker, workflow_id=None, *, resend_on_transient_err=False) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]]
- start_workflow_async(spec, broker, workflow_id=None, *, resend_on_transient_err=False) -> WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]]
- Standalone functions (alternative to spec.start())
- Returns Ok(WorkflowHandle) on success, Err(WorkflowStartError) on failure
- resend_on_transient_err: auto-retry up to 3 times on transient infra errors with exponential backoff

### WorkflowStartResult[T] (workflow start Result type)
- spec.start() / start_async() / start_workflow() / start_workflow_async() return WorkflowStartResult[WorkflowHandle[T]]
- WorkflowStartResult[T] = Result[T, WorkflowStartError]
- Ok(WorkflowHandle): workflow created and root tasks enqueued
- Err(WorkflowStartError): start failed; match on the variant
- WorkflowStartError is a union of frozen variants; every variant has code (WorkflowStartErrorCode), message (str), retryable (bool), workflow_name (str), workflow_id (str, the id this start used)
- Variants: WorkflowStartBrokerNotConfigured; WorkflowStartValidationFailed (exception: BaseException | NoCause); WorkflowStartIdConflict (existing_workflow_name: str); WorkflowStartCommandConflict; WorkflowStartEnqueueFailed (retryable = the core's classification, exception: BaseException); WorkflowStartAsyncContext
- WorkflowStartErrorCode: BROKER_NOT_CONFIGURED, VALIDATION_FAILED, WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT, WORKFLOW_COMMAND_CONFLICT, ENQUEUE_FAILED, ASYNC_CONTEXT
- WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT: the workflow id exists for another workflow name; nothing was written; use another id
- WORKFLOW_COMMAND_CONFLICT: the workflow id holds a workflow of the same name that another start command started, or a sub-workflow; nothing was written; never retryable; retry_start refuses it; send the same start command or use another id
- A start with an existing workflow_id: same name and same start command returns the existing handle; runs started before this release have no stored start command and are not checked
- ENQUEUE_FAILED: schema init or the start transaction failed with a database or driver error; any other exception in the start transaction propagates
- retryable=True: transient (DB connection blip), retryable=False: permanent (validation, config error)
- Use is_ok(result) / is_err(result) type guards, or result.ok_value to extract handle

### ExceptionMapper
- Type: dict[type[BaseException], str]
- Maps exception classes to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE error codes
- Exact class matching only (no MRO/inheritance lookup)
- Resolution order: task_mapper -> global_mapper -> task_default -> global_default
- Global: AppConfig(exception_mapper={ValueError: "VALIDATION_ERROR"})
- Per-task: @app.task("name", exception_mapper={TimeoutError: "TIMEOUT"})

### RetryPolicy
- RetryPolicy.fixed(intervals, *, auto_retry_for, jitter) e.g. RetryPolicy.fixed([60, 120, 300], auto_retry_for=["ERROR_CODE", ...]); the length of intervals is the retry count
- RetryPolicy.exponential(base_seconds, *, max_retries, auto_retry_for, jitter, max_delay_seconds=None)
- auto_retry_for: required list of error codes that trigger retries
- jitter: bool (default True, adds a random 0-25% to each delay; never shortens)
- Exponential: exactly one base interval, delay = base * 2^(attempt-1)

### RecoveryConfig
- auto_requeue_stale_claimed: bool (default True)
- claimed_stale_threshold_ms: int (default 120_000, range 1s-1hr)
- auto_fail_stale_running: bool (default True)
- running_stale_threshold_ms: int (default 300_000, range 1s-2hr)
- check_interval_ms: int (default 30_000, range 1s-10min)
- runner_heartbeat_interval_ms: int (default 30_000, range 1s-2min)
- claimer_heartbeat_interval_ms: int (default 30_000, range 1s-2min)
- auto_terminate_orphaned_workflow_tasks: bool (default True)
- finalizing_stale_threshold_ms: int (default 300_000, range 1s-2hr)
- crashed_worker_recovery_grace_ms: int (default 10_000, range 0-1hr; 0 disables)
- orphan_task_audit_interval_ms: int (default 60_000, range 1s-24hr)
- worker_state_snapshot_interval_ms: int (default 30_000, range 1s-1min; the cap is half the 120 s live window WORKER_STATE_LIVE_WINDOW_S, so a running worker stays live when a snapshot write is late by up to half the window; a larger value fails with HRS-204)
- phase2_quarantine_after_attempts: int (default 25, range 3-1000)
- workflow_recovery_failure_limit: int (default 25, range 3-1000; reaper passes in which the recovery of a workflow may raise a persistent error before the workflow fails with WORKFLOW_RECOVERY_LIMIT_REACHED)
- Constraint: stale thresholds must be >= 2x heartbeat intervals; with auto_fail_stale_running=True, running_stale_threshold_ms >= 2 x (runner_heartbeat_interval_ms + 2000) (the worker stops when no runner heartbeat lands for half of it; HRS-204 below)
- Retention fields are not on RecoveryConfig; setting heartbeat_retention_hours (removed in 0.5.0) or a retention field here fails at construction

### RetentionConfig
- Reached as AppConfig.retention
- paused_workflow_auto_cancel_after: timedelta | None (default None; a positive duration of at most 365,000 days, else HRS-216)
- worker_state_retention_hours: int | None (default 168 / 7 days, range 1-8760, None disables pruning)
- terminal_record_retention_hours: int | None (default 720 / 30 days, range 1-43800, None disables pruning; applies to terminal workflow rows)
- history_leaf_horizon_days: int (default 3, range 2-14)
- heartbeat_leaf_horizon_hours: int (default 6, range 2-48)
- partition_maintenance_interval_s: int (default 900, range 60-3600)
- retention_sweep_interval_s: int (default 300, range 30s-24h)
- retention_delete_batch_size: int (default 500, range 50-10000)
- retention_periods: tuple[timedelta, ...] (default (); whole days 1-1825; periods a send may choose explicitly)
- queue_retention: dict[str, timedelta | None] (default {}; whole days 1-1825, or None for forever; the class key is standard_<days>d)
- Terminal task records are removed by partition drop, not by row delete

### WorkerResilienceConfig
- db_retry_initial_ms: int (default 500, range 100ms-60s)
- db_retry_max_ms: int (default 30_000, range 500ms-5min)
- db_retry_max_attempts: int (default 0 = infinite, range 0-10_000)
- notify_poll_interval_ms: int (default 5_000, range 1s-5min)
- Constraint: db_retry_max_ms >= db_retry_initial_ms

### discover_tasks
- app.discover_tasks(["myapp.tasks", "myapp.workflows"])
- Imports exact entries listed (dotted modules via importlib, .py paths via path import)
- Export decorated functions from __init__.py or list submodules explicitly

### Scheduling Models

#### Weekday (enum)
- MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY, FRIDAY, SATURDAY, SUNDAY

#### IntervalSchedule
- IntervalSchedule(seconds=30) | IntervalSchedule(hours=1, minutes=30)
- At least one of: seconds, minutes, hours, days

#### HourlySchedule
- HourlySchedule(minute=30, second=0) -> every hour at XX:30:00

#### DailySchedule
- DailySchedule(time=time(3, 0, 0)) -> daily at 03:00:00

#### WeeklySchedule
- WeeklySchedule(days=[Weekday.MONDAY, Weekday.FRIDAY], time=time(9, 0))

#### MonthlySchedule
- MonthlySchedule(day=15, time=time(15, 0)) -> 15th at 15:00

#### CronSchedule
- Typed 5-field cron-style schedule (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week); fires at second :00
- Fields: minute=list[term] (0-59), hour=list[term] (0-23), month=list[enum_term] (Month), day=DaySelector
- Numeric terms: CronEvery() | CronStep(step=n) (*/n anchored at domain start) | CronValues(values=[...]) | CronRange(start, end, step=1)
- Enum terms (parameterized [Month]/[Weekday]): CronEvery() | CronEnumStep[T](step=n) | CronEnumValues[T](values=[...]) | CronEnumRange[T](start, end, step=1)
- DaySelector: EveryDay() | ByMonthDay(day_of_month=[...]) | ByWeekday(day_of_week=[...]) | EitherDay(dom, dow) (OR) | BothDays(dom, dow) (AND)
- Wall-clock aligned (unlike IntervalSchedule). CronStep(step=4) on hour -> 0,4,8,12,16,20
- Example: CronSchedule(minute=[CronValues(values=[15])], hour=[CronStep(step=4)], month=[CronEvery()], day=EveryDay()) -> every 4h at :15
- Validation (ConfigurationError at construction): per-field domain, range start<=end (no wrap), step <= field span, month/day-of-month satisfiability
- Month enum: JANUARY..DECEMBER (str values "january".."december")

#### SchedulePattern
- Type union: IntervalSchedule | HourlySchedule | DailySchedule | WeeklySchedule | MonthlySchedule | CronSchedule

#### TaskSchedule
- name: str (unique schedule identifier)
- task_name: str (registered task name)
- pattern: SchedulePattern
- kwargs: dict (task keyword arguments; schedules are kwargs-only)
- queue_name: str | None
- enabled: bool (default True)
- timezone: str (default "UTC")
- catch_up_missed: bool (default False)
- max_catch_up_runs: int (default 100, 1-10000)

#### ScheduleConfig
- enabled: bool (default True)
- schedules: list[TaskSchedule]
- check_interval_seconds: int (default 1, range 1-60)

### horsies check (CLI validation)
- Run `horsies check` before deploys — it lists all blocking errors in one pass
- Use as a feedback loop from the library during development: define tasks/workflows, run check, fix errors, repeat
- `horsies check <module> [--live]` — validate without starting services
- Runs app.check(live=...) which performs phased validation:
  - Phase 1: Config validation (implicit at AppConfig construction), including every worker profile (HRS-218, with the profile name and field path)
  - Phase 2: Task module imports — imports each module, collects import/definition errors
  - Phase 3: Workflow validation — triggered during imports (WorkflowSpec DAG construction)
  - Phase 3.1: WorkflowDefinition class validation — imported definitions must declare definition_key
  - Phase 3.2: Workflow builders — executes @app.workflow_builder functions under send suppression and validates returned specs
  - Phase 3.3: Undecorated builder detection (HRS-030)
  - Phase 3.5: Runtime policy safety — validates retry/exception-mapper policy metadata
  - Phase 3.6: Schedule validation — validates timezone, task registration, queue, and the kwargs wire contract of each enabled schedule; skipped for the worker role
  - Phase 4 (--live only): Broker connectivity — async SELECT 1 against PostgreSQL
  - Phase 4.1 (--live only): Worker connections — each worker profile against max_connections less reserved slots (HRS-219); skipped with no profiles or with pgbouncer_transaction_mode=True
- Guarantee model:
  - Strong: @app.workflow_builder decorated functions are fully executed and validated for exercised builder cases
  - Best-effort: undecorated builder detection (HRS-030) is heuristic — only scans directly discovered modules
- Returns list[HorsiesError]; empty = all passed
- Errors are collected within each phase; check returns early before later phases when earlier phases fail
- Worker and scheduler also run check() at startup before accepting work
- On success: prints "ok: all validations passed" with task count, then "declared error codes:" with one line per declaring task ("<task>: CODE, CODE"), or "declared error codes: none"
- On failure: prints Rust-style ValidationReport to stderr, exits with code 1

### Error Types and Reporting

#### HorsiesErrorCode (enum, startup/validation errors HRS-001-HRS-399)
Workflow validation (HRS-001-HRS-099):
<!-- members: HorsiesErrorCode part -->
- HRS-001 WORKFLOW_NO_NAME
- HRS-002 WORKFLOW_NO_NODES
- HRS-003 WORKFLOW_INVALID_NODE_ID
- HRS-004 WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE_NODE_ID
- HRS-005 WORKFLOW_NO_ROOT_TASKS
- HRS-006 WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEPENDENCY
- HRS-007 WORKFLOW_CYCLE_DETECTED
- HRS-008 WORKFLOW_INVALID_ARGS_FROM
- HRS-009 WORKFLOW_INVALID_CONTEXT_FROM
- HRS-010 WORKFLOW_CONTEXT_PARAMETER_MISSING
- HRS-011 WORKFLOW_INVALID_OUTPUT
- HRS-012 WORKFLOW_INVALID_SUCCESS_POLICY
- HRS-013 WORKFLOW_INVALID_JOIN
- HRS-014 WORKFLOW_UNRESOLVED_QUEUE
- HRS-015 WORKFLOW_UNRESOLVED_PRIORITY
- HRS-016 WORKFLOW_NO_DEFINITION_KEY
- HRS-017 WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE_DEFINITION_KEY
- HRS-018 WORKFLOW_SUBWORKFLOW_APP_MISSING
- HRS-019 WORKFLOW_INVALID_KWARG_KEY
- HRS-020 WORKFLOW_MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMS
- HRS-021 WORKFLOW_KWARGS_ARGS_FROM_OVERLAP
- HRS-022 WORKFLOW_SUBWORKFLOW_PARAMS_REQUIRE_BUILD_WITH
- HRS-024 WORKFLOW_ARGS_FROM_TYPE_MISMATCH
- HRS-025 WORKFLOW_OUTPUT_TYPE_MISMATCH
- HRS-026 WORKFLOW_POSITIONAL_ARGS_NOT_SUPPORTED
- HRS-027 WORKFLOW_CHECK_CASES_REQUIRED
- HRS-028 WORKFLOW_CHECK_CASE_INVALID
- HRS-029 WORKFLOW_CHECK_BUILDER_EXCEPTION
- HRS-030 WORKFLOW_CHECK_UNDECORATED_BUILDER
- HRS-031 WORKFLOW_KWARGS_NOT_SERIALIZABLE
- HRS-032 WORKFLOW_INVALID_ID
- HRS-033 WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEFINITION_CONFIG
- HRS-034 WORKFLOW_INVALID_PRIORITY
- HRS-035 WORKFLOW_NAIVE_GOOD_UNTIL
- HRS-036 WORKFLOW_SUBWORKFLOW_DEPTH_LIMIT
- HRS-037 WORKFLOW_SUBWORKFLOW_SELF_NESTING
- HRS-038 WORKFLOW_TOO_MANY_NODES
Task definition (HRS-100-HRS-199):
<!-- members: HorsiesErrorCode part -->
- HRS-100 TASK_NO_RETURN_TYPE
- HRS-101 TASK_INVALID_RETURN_TYPE
- HRS-102 TASK_INVALID_OPTIONS
- HRS-103 TASK_INVALID_QUEUE
- HRS-104 TASK_PREDECORATED_NOT_SUPPORTED (the task function is pre-decorated: it has a __wrapped__ chain)
- HRS-105 TASK_STRICT_SIGNATURE_VIOLATION
- HRS-107 TASK_SHARED_ASYNC_REQUIRES_ASYNC_DEF (execution=SHARED_ASYNC on a def function)
- HRS-108 TASK_SHARED_THREAD_REQUIRES_DEF (execution=SHARED_THREAD on an async def function)
- HRS-109 TASK_SHARED_EXECUTION_REQUIRES_TIMEOUT (SHARED_ASYNC or SHARED_THREAD without timeout_ms)
- HRS-110 TASK_CANCEL_GRACE_REQUIRES_SHARED_ASYNC (cancel_grace_ms with execution=SHARED_THREAD)
- HRS-111 TASK_CANCEL_GRACE_OUT_OF_RANGE (cancel_grace_ms outside 100 to 10000 ms)
- HRS-112 TASK_INVALID_ERROR_CODE (an error_codes entry is empty, not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, or an exception class name)
- HRS-113 TASK_DUPLICATE_ERROR_CODE (an error_codes entry is given twice)
Config/broker (HRS-200-HRS-299):
<!-- members: HorsiesErrorCode part -->
- HRS-200 CONFIG_INVALID_QUEUE_MODE
- HRS-201 CONFIG_INVALID_CLUSTER_CAP
- HRS-202 CONFIG_INVALID_PREFETCH
- HRS-203 DATABASE_INVALID_URL
- HRS-204 CONFIG_INVALID_RECOVERY
- HRS-205 CONFIG_INVALID_SCHEDULE
- HRS-206 CLI_INVALID_ARGS
- HRS-207 WORKER_INVALID_LOCATOR
- HRS-208 CONFIG_INVALID_RESILIENCE
- HRS-209 CONFIG_INVALID_EXCEPTION_MAPPER
- HRS-210 MODULE_IMPORT_ERROR
- HRS-211 DATABASE_INIT_FAILED
- HRS-212 CHECK_RESERVED_CODE_COLLISION (exception_mapper/default_unhandled_error_code collides with built-in code; an error_codes entry is a built-in code or WORKFLOW_STOPPED)
- HRS-213 CONFIG_INVALID_DATABASE_POOL
- HRS-214 CONFIG_INVALID_CHILD_HOOK
- HRS-215 CONFIG_INVALID_KEEPALIVE
- HRS-216 CONFIG_INVALID_RETENTION
- HRS-217 CHECK_LIVE_ASYNC_CONTEXT (check(live=True) called inside a running event loop; the live check did not run)
- HRS-218 CONFIG_INVALID_WORKER_PROFILE (a worker profile is not valid; the message names the profile and the field path)
- HRS-219 CHECK_WORKER_CONNECTIONS (check(live=True): one worker of a profile opens more Postgres connections itself than the server allows, or the limit could not be read; not compared, but stated in the error: task code that sends opens the task_send_pool of its child kind in its child per event loop it sends from)
- HRS-220 CONFIG_OTEL_API_MISSING (AppConfig(tracing=OtelTracing()) and the OpenTelemetry API is not installed; install horsies[otel])
- HRS-221 CONFIG_INVALID_TRACE_LINK (a TraceLinkTemplate of MonitoringUIConfig that the core refuses: not an http or https URL with a host, not exactly one {trace_id}, another brace, a byte outside printable ASCII, or more than 2,048 bytes)
- HRS-222 EVENT_HANDLER_UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE (app.on_event(value): value is not an event type of horsies.telemetry)
- HRS-223 EVENT_HANDLER_INVALID_SIGNATURE (the handler is not a function or a bound method, is a generator function, does not take one event, or annotates its event parameter with another event type)
- HRS-224 EVENT_HANDLER_DUPLICATE_NAME (an earlier handler has the same name, module.qualname of its function)
- HRS-225 EVENT_HANDLER_INVALID_NAME (the function has no module name, or its name is longer than 255 characters)
- HRS-226 EVENT_HANDLER_LIMIT (the app has 32 event handlers already)
- HRS-227 CONFIG_INVALID_PAYLOAD (a payload size bound, warn_bytes or reject_bytes, is not valid; only the Rust and TypeScript clients raise it, Python's PayloadPolicy refuses the value through its field bounds)
Registry (HRS-300-HRS-399):
<!-- members: HorsiesErrorCode part -->
- HRS-300 TASK_NOT_REGISTERED
- HRS-301 TASK_DUPLICATE_NAME
- HRS-302 WORKFLOW_UNREGISTERED_TASK (a workflow node names a task that the app of its workflow builder does not register; the Rust client raises it at builder.task(node), and the node is not added)

#### HorsiesError (base exception)
- Rust-style formatted error display (like rustc compiler errors)
- Fields: message, code (HorsiesErrorCode | None), location (SourceLocation | None), notes (list[str]), help_text (str | None)
- .format_diagnostic(use_colors=None) -> str (ANSI-colored for TTY)
- Auto-detects source location from call stack (first frame outside horsies internals)
- Subclasses: WorkflowValidationError, ConfigurationError, TaskDefinitionError, RegistryError
- Environment variables:
  - HORSIES_FORCE_COLOR=1: force ANSI colors even when not TTY
  - NO_COLOR: disable ANSI colors (https://no-color.org/)

#### SourceLocation
- .file -> str, .line -> int, .column -> int | None
- .get_source_line() -> str | None (reads actual source for display)
- .format_short() -> str ("file:line" or "file:line:col")
- SourceLocation.from_function(fn) -> SourceLocation | None

#### ValidationReport
- Collects multiple HorsiesError instances within a validation phase
- ValidationReport(phase_name: str)
- .add(error: HorsiesError), .has_errors() -> bool, .errors -> list[HorsiesError]
- .format_diagnostic() -> str (formats all errors with "aborting due to N errors" summary)
- Used by WorkflowSpec construction, AppConfig validation, and app.check()

#### raise_collected(report: ValidationReport) -> None
- 0 errors: no-op (returns normally)
- 1 error: raises the original HorsiesError (preserves except clauses)
- 2+ errors: raises MultipleValidationErrors wrapping the report

#### MultipleValidationErrors (extends HorsiesError)
- Wraps a ValidationReport with 2+ errors
- .report -> ValidationReport
- .format_diagnostic() delegates to report

#### WorkflowContextMissingId (RuntimeError)
- Raised when TaskNode/NodeKey has no node_id for WorkflowContext.result_for()

### Serialization
- Supported: primitives, dict, list, Pydantic BaseModel, dataclass, datetime, date, time
- Pydantic models: model_dump(mode="json") -> model_validate() round-trip
- datetime: ISO 8601 with timezone preservation
- Pydantic/dataclass values rehydrate to instances; plain dicts remain dicts
- Unsupported: custom classes, __main__-defined classes, lambdas, file handles

### Failure Semantics
- Default (join="all", allow_failed_dependencies=False): downstream SKIPPED when any dep fails/skips
- allow_failed_dependencies=True: downstream runs, receives Failed(task_error)
- join="any"/"quorum": downstream can still run if success threshold met
- SKIPPED cascades for join="all" with allow_failed_dependencies=False
- OnError.FAIL (default): store error, continue DAG, mark FAILED when all terminal
- OnError.PAUSE: immediately pause, block new enqueues, await resume

### Utilities
- slugify(value: str) -> str: convert string to valid node_id ([A-Za-z0-9_\-:.]+)

### Terminal State Constants
- TASK_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset[TaskStatus] = {COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED}
- WORKFLOW_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset[WorkflowStatus] = {COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED}
- WORKFLOW_TASK_TERMINAL_STATES: frozenset[WorkflowTaskStatus] = {COMPLETED, FAILED, SKIPPED}

### CLI Commands
- `horsies worker <module> --profile NAME [--loglevel LEVEL] [--metrics-listen HOST:PORT]`
  - `--profile NAME` — required; a profile in AppConfig.worker_profiles; no default profile; a missing or unknown name exits 1 and lists the defined names
  - Worker settings live in the profile, not in flags: WorkerProfile(isolated=IsolatedChildren(count=N, recycle=IsolatedRecycle(after=TaskLimit(tasks=N) | NoTaskLimit(), above=MemoryLimit(mb=N) | NoMemoryLimit())), shared_async=SharedAsyncChildren(count=N, seats=K), shared_thread=SharedThreadChildren(count=N, seats=K), claim=ClaimLimits(per_queue_per_pass=..., claimed_per_worker=...), drain_timeout=timedelta, preload=ChildPreload.LIBRARY | APP | NONE)
  - Removed PostgresConfig fields fail at config build (HRS-213): worker_child_pool_min_size -> IsolatedPool/SharedPool min_size; worker_child_pool_max_size -> max_size=PoolSize(connections=N); worker_child_pool_check -> check; worker_pool_size, worker_max_overflow -> WorkerProfile(pool=ParentPool(max_size=PoolSize(connections=N))) for the worker process and task_send_pool=PoolSize(connections=N) on a child kind for task code that sends
  - Removed flags exit 2 and name the field: --processes -> IsolatedChildren.count; --max-tasks-per-child -> IsolatedRecycle.after; --max-memory-per-child-mb -> IsolatedRecycle.above; --max-claim-batch -> ClaimLimits.per_queue_per_pass; --max-claim-per-worker -> ClaimLimits.claimed_per_worker; --drain-timeout -> WorkerProfile.drain_timeout; --child-preload -> WorkerProfile.preload
  - Boot warns (never refuses) when count x MemoryLimit.mb is above the usable memory: the cgroup limit (the group that /proc/self/cgroup names, v1 memory group else v2 group; the smallest memory.limit_in_bytes / memory.max of the group and its parents, so a systemd MemoryMax or --cgroupns=host counts; without /proc/self/cgroup the files at the mount point; "max" or no file = no limit) when below the host RAM, else the host RAM; the warning names the source ("container limit" or "host RAM"), and when one worker opens more Postgres connections itself than the server has usable slots; a memory limit at or below the warmed child baseline still refuses to start
  - `--metrics-listen HOST:PORT` (or [IPV6]:PORT; no default, no config field) serves GET /metrics (Prometheus text 0.0.4), GET /livez (503 only when the claim loop is stuck) and GET /readyz (200 when the pools have no failure, a child serves and the liveness lock is held); a bad value exits 2; a bind failure does not stop the worker. See /horsies/observability/metrics/
- `horsies scheduler <module> [--loglevel LEVEL]`
- `horsies check <module> [--live] [--loglevel LEVEL]`
- `horsies web <module> [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--auth none|trusted-header] [--trusted-header HEADER] [--enable-actions] [--trace-link TEMPLATE] [--loglevel LEVEL]` — serve the monitoring web UI (requires the `horsies[web]` extra)
  - `horsies web --database-url URL [--session-database-url URL] [--pgbouncer-transaction-mode] [...]` — monitor a database without importing an app module (registry-less)
  - Pass either `<module>` or `--database-url`, not both
  - Defaults: `--host 127.0.0.1`, `--port 8600`, `--auth none`, `--trusted-header X-Forwarded-User`, actions off (view-only)
  - `--auth none` is allowed only on a loopback host; a non-loopback host requires `--auth trusted-header`
  - `--enable-actions` allows cancel/pause/resume
  - `--trace-link TEMPLATE` links a task's trace id in the task detail: an http or https URL with one {trace_id} (MonitoringUIConfig(trace_link=TraceLinkTemplate(template=...)) when mounting; a refused template is HRS-221 CONFIG_INVALID_TRACE_LINK)
- `horsies metrics <module> --listen HOST:PORT [--loglevel LEVEL]` — serve the fleet metrics of the app's database at GET /metrics (Prometheus text 0.0.4); `--listen` is required (HOST:PORT or [IPV6]:PORT); reads at start, then at most once per 15 s, each statement within 2 s; a failed query has no series and sets horsies_exporter_collect_failed{query} 1; exit 2 bad address, 0 on SIGTERM/SIGINT, 1 when the app does not load or the address does not bind. `horsies web` and create_monitoring_app also serve GET /metrics behind can_view. See /horsies/observability/fleet-collector/
- `horsies get-docs [--output DIR] [--ref main]` — fetch the docs of the installed version's release tag for AI agents (default: .horsies-docs/); a development version has no tag and fails unless `--ref main` is given
- `horsies skills install --target DIR [--force]` — copy the packaged skill folder to `DIR/horsies/`; refuses to replace a changed copy without `--force`
- Module format: `myapp.config:app` (dotted:attr) or `app/config.py:app` (file:attr)
- Auto-discovery: if module has exactly one Horsies instance, `:name` can be omitted
- Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = error (also a missing or unknown --profile, and a worker that cannot write runner heartbeats), 2 = bad invocation (argument error, a removed worker flag), 77 = a worker that cannot write runner heartbeats and has not stopped 120 s later
- Signals: SIGTERM/SIGINT for graceful shutdown (workers wait up to the profile's drain_timeout (default 300 seconds) for running tasks, then kill their children)
- Both worker and scheduler run app.check() at startup; fail with ValidationReport if errors

### Observability

### Operations

### Migrations
- Migrating to 0.1.2 -- strict-serde breaking changes from 0.1.1 -> /horsies/migrations/migration-to-0-1-2/
- Migrating to 0.5.0 and 0.5.2 -- live/history split (schema v34), offline cutover, offline schema v35 upgrade -> /horsies/migrations/migration-to-0-5-0/
- Migrating to 0.6.0 -- stop-all upgrade rule, schema v52, new settings and flags, required code changes -> /horsies/migrations/migration-to-0-6-0/
- Migrating to 0.7.0 -- upgrade order: psycopg 3.3.7, worker profiles and the flag to field table, new error code cases, refused result waits inside a task, workflow limits, stop 0.6.x workers before schema v55, exit codes, behaviour changes -> /horsies/migrations/migration-to-0-7-0/
- Migrating to 0.8.0 -- upgrade order: the database URL without +psycopg (HRS-203), the connection settings that the core reads, the native extension, drain 0.7 and start on a new database, task ids as uuid.UUID, the class of a database failure, ForkedAfterCoreStart and CoreStopped, removed and changed members, new config bounds, web API clients, the worker liveness lock and exit code 79 -> /horsies/migrations/migration-to-0-8-0/
